mainTopic: צרורות (pebble damage): the dispute of סומכוס and רבנן, questions about שינוי and כח כחו, and pebbles kicked up in רשות הרבים.
overview: The amud begins by explaining why the ברייתא gives נזק שלם for a rooster that broke a vessel while רב יוסף gives only חצי נזק. The גמרא's answer is that this is the known מחלוקת between סומכוס and רבנן about צרורות, and that seeds in the vessel made the rooster's act normal. רב אשי then asks two questions about צרורות. The first is whether unusual behavior (שינוי) lowers the payment to רביע נזק. The second is whether, according to סומכוס, כח כחו counts like כחו. Both end in תיקו. Next the גמרא asks how to read the משנה's line about kicking and pebbles. It proves from the shard case in the סיפא that the משנה follows רבנן, and it shows that רב אשי's quarter-damage question is really about this line. Further questions follow: an animal that cannot avoid scattering pebbles, and pebbles kicked up in רשות הרבים. On the second, רבי זירא rules that they are a תולדה of רגל and exempt there. Twice רבי ירמיה challenges him from sources, and twice רבי זירא retracts his claim that pebbles flung in רשות הרבים which damage in רשות היחיד are exempt. The amud ends as רבי ירמיה opens yet another challenge, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Suggesting the dispute is about warning for pebble damage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the ברייתא (נזק שלם) and רב יוסף (חצי נזק) argue about whether העדאה works for צרורות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this what they argue about? One holds there is העדאה for צרורות, and the other holds there is no העדאה for צרורות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible explanation for why the two sources give different payments for the crowing rooster.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says נזק שלם, which would make sense if the rooster did this several times and became a מועד. רב יוסף says חצי נזק, which would mean that repeating the act never raises צרורות to full payment. If this is right, the two sources are simply arguing about העדאה.

keyTerms.meaning: they argue
the warning given after an animal does something repeatedly, which makes its owner pay more
one Sage... and the other Sage

phrases.english: And is it about this that they argue:
phrases.notes: "They" are the ברייתא of רמי בר יחזקאל, which says full damages, and רב יוסף, who says half.

phrases.english: one Sage holds there is forewarning (for pebbles),
and the other Sage holds there is no forewarning?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion contrasting the ברייתא with רב יוסף's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the difference between נזק שלם and חצי נזק a dispute about whether העדאה applies to צרורות?

steps.title: No, it was one time, and this is the dispute of סומכוס and רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. The case can be a single incident, and the two sources follow the known מחלוקת between סומכוס and רבנן about צרורות.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The case is one time only, and they argue about the same thing that סומכוס and the רבנן argue about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 1 and gives a different reason for the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need to say the rooster did this repeatedly. סומכוס holds that צרורות always pay נזק שלם, and the רבנן hold they pay חצי נזק. The ברייתא follows סומכוס and רב יוסף follows the רבנן, even for a single time.

keyTerms.meaning: one time
a dispute
a תנא who holds that צרורות pay full damages

phrases.english: No; it is about one time,
and they argue about the dispute of Sumakhos and the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; בְּחַד זִמְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the העדאה explanation from step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects that the dispute must be about העדאה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case need not involve repeated acts. The known סומכוס and רבנן dispute explains the difference even for one incident.

steps.title: But isn't this unusual behavior?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a rooster sticking its head into a glass vessel is unusual (משונה), so how could anyone say נזק שלם?
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is unusual behavior!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new explanation from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סומכוס gives full payment for normal צרורות. Unusual behavior belongs to קרן, which pays חצי נזק. If putting a head into a vessel is unusual, even סומכוס should not give נזק שלם.

keyTerms.meaning: unusual behavior for the animal, treated like קרן
but isn't it...? (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: But it is unusual!
phrases.notes: He means the rooster pushing its head into a glass vessel. Animals don't normally do that.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מְשׁוּנֶּה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא's נזק שלם follows סומכוס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unusual acts fall under קרן and pay half, so full payment cannot be explained by סומכוס.

steps.title: There were seeds in the vessel
steps.stepSummary: The answer: there were seeds inside, so it is normal for a rooster to put its head in.
steps.simpleTranslation: The vessel had seeds in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by describing the case more exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rooster normally reaches in after food. With seeds inside, putting its head in is normal behavior, not משונה. So the case stays regular צרורות, and סומכוס's נזק שלם can apply.

keyTerms.meaning: seeds
that there is in it

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא (נזק שלם) and רב יוסף (חצי נזק) can be read as the סומכוס and רבנן dispute about one normal act, since seeds made the rooster's behavior normal.

phrases.english: Where there were seeds in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִית בֵּיהּ בִּזְרָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rooster's act seemed unusual, so it looked like קרן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Seeds were inside, so the act is normal and counts as regular צרורות.

steps.title: רב אשי asks: do unusual pebbles pay one-quarter?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether unusual צרורות lower the payment from חצי נזק to רביע נזק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: If an animal kicks up pebbles in an unusual way, does that matter, so the owner pays only a quarter of the damage? Or does it not matter?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens: does unusual behavior change the payment for צרורות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normal צרורות pay half. For normal damage, unusual behavior (קרן) cuts the payment in half. רב אשי asks whether the same cut applies to צרורות, which would bring them down to a quarter.

keyTerms.meaning: asks (a question he cannot answer yet)
a change from the animal's normal behavior
pebbles an animal kicks up that cause damage
one-quarter of the damage

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides of the question mention רביע נזק. The question is whether שינוי makes any difference for צרורות, which would mean paying a quarter. Only the first side actually leads to a quarter payment.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
Is there deviation for pebbles, to pay one-quarter of the damage,
phrases.notes: "Deviation" means the animal acted in an unusual way. If that counts, the owner pays only a quarter.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין שִׁנּוּי לִצְרוֹרוֹת לִרְבִיעַ נֶזֶק?
phrases.english: or is there no deviation for pebbles, to pay one-quarter of the damage?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question, still about צרורות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does unusual behavior reduce the payment for צרורות to רביע נזק?

steps.title: Answered from רבא's question: no quarter payment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רב אשי from רבא's question about העדאה for צרורות. That question shows that unusual behavior does not lower צרורות to a quarter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Answer him from רבא. רבא asked whether there is העדאה for צרורות or not. This shows there is no reduction for unusual behavior.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to settle רב אשי's question using how רבא framed his own question. The next step rejects this proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: העדאה applies to unusual behavior that becomes a pattern. רבא asks whether העדאה raises צרורות to full payment, which assumes unusual צרורות start at half. If unusual צרורות paid only a quarter, העדאה would only raise them to half, and רבא's question would not make sense as he asked it. So שינוי does not reduce צרורות.

keyTerms.meaning: resolve the question
from the implication
an אמורא whose question is used here as proof

steps.whatToRemember: This step proposes that unusual behavior does not lower צרורות to רביע נזק, based on the way רבא asked his question about העדאה. The next step knocks down this proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא tries to learn an answer from the way another אמורא framed his question. The next step shows why that kind of proof can fail.

phrases.english: Resolve it for him from Rava,
for Rava asked:
Is there forewarning for pebbles,
or is there no forewarning for pebbles?
By implication, there is no deviation.
phrases.notes: His question only works if unusual pebbles already pay half. Warning could then raise them to full.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּפְשׁוֹט לֵיהּ מִדְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no שינוי for צרורות. Unusual צרורות still pay חצי נזק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's question about העדאה for צרורות

steps.title: רבא's question may have been an 'if you say' question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from רבא. Maybe רבא was asking his העדאה question only on the assumption that unusual behavior makes no difference. So רב אשי's question remains unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe רבא was speaking in an 'if you will say' style: if you will say that unusual behavior makes no difference, then is there העדאה or not? The question stays unresolved (תיקו).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 6. It says רבא's question does not have to show that unusual behavior makes no difference for צרורות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6, the גמרא assumed that רבא's question about העדאה only makes sense if unusual behavior never lowers צרורות to רביע נזק. Now it says רבא may have been asking 'if you assume that,' without deciding it himself. Once that is possible, the proof is gone, and רב אשי's question ends with תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you will say': asking a question on top of an assumption, without deciding that the assumption is true
Unusual or out-of-the-ordinary behavior by the animal
Forewarning: the animal does something three times, so its owner pays more from then on
'Let it stand': the question stays unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying that unusual behavior makes no difference. He is only asking: IF it makes no difference, what happens with העדאה? That is why his question cannot prove anything for רב אשי.

phrases.english: Perhaps Rava was speaking in the style of 'if you will say' –
phrases.notes: He means רבא was building his question on an assumption, not ruling on it.

phrases.english: if you will say that there is no [effect of] unusual behavior,
is there forewarning, or is there no forewarning?
Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's question (does unusual צרורות drop to רביע נזק?) ends unresolved, because רבא's question may have been only an 'if you say' question.
steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא רָבָא אִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes apart the answer given in Step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבא's question about העדאה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא's question could be built on an assumed premise ('if you say'), so it does not show what רבא himself held about unusual צרורות

steps.title: רב אשי asks about כח כחו according to סומכוס
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks: according to סומכוס, is damage done by כח כחו (a force created by a force) treated like damage done by the animal's direct force?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: according to סומכוס, is the force of its force like its force, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks a new question about צרורות according to סומכוס. Is damage that is one more step removed from the animal treated the same as regular pebble damage?
steps.deeperAnalysis: סומכוס holds that regular צרורות (the animal's own force) pay נזק שלם. רב אשי asks about a case one step further away, כח כחו, where the force that did the damage was itself set in motion by the animal's force. Does that more distant force still count like כחו?

keyTerms.meaning: Asks or raises a question
The force of its force: damage two steps removed from the animal
Is it like its own force?
The תנא who holds that צרורות pay full damage

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
according to Sumchos, the force of its force,
phrases.notes: Regular pebbles are the animal's own force; here something those pebbles set moving did the damage.

phrases.english: is it like its force, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי כֹּחַ כֹּחוֹ לְסוֹמְכוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first question ends in תיקו, רב אשי opens a new question about צרורות
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, according to סומכוס, כח כחו has the same status as כחו (full payment)

steps.title: The two sides of רב אשי's question, left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the two sides. Maybe סומכוס did receive the הלכה of half damage for pebbles and applies it only to כח כחו. Or maybe he did not receive that הלכה at all. The question ends in תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he receive a tradition (הלכה) and apply it to the force of its force? Or perhaps he did not receive the tradition at all? Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what is behind רב אשי's question. Then it ends with תיקו, without deciding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known הלכה, a received tradition, that pebble damage pays חצי נזק. סומכוס cannot apply it to regular pebbles, since he holds they pay full. So perhaps he did have the tradition and applies it to כח כחו, which would then pay half. Or perhaps he never received it, in which case even כח כחו pays full.

keyTerms.meaning: A received tradition, here that pebble damage pays half
Learned or received (a tradition)
He applies it to (a specific case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא tries to fit a known tradition into the view of a תנא who seems to disagree with it, by finding a narrower case where the tradition could still apply.

phrases.english: Did he receive a tradition –
phrases.notes: 'He' is סומכוס. The tradition is that pebble damage pays only half.

phrases.english: and he applies it to the force of its force,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא לָא גְּמִיר הֲלָכָה כְּלָל?
phrases.english: or perhaps he did not receive the tradition at all?
Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.whatToRemember: According to סומכוס, whether כח כחו pays half or full depends on whether he accepted the pebble tradition at all. The question stays תיקו.
steps.triggerLanguage: מִי גְּמִיר הֲלָכָה וּמוֹקֵי לַהּ בְּכֹחַ כֹּחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind both sides of רב אשי's question from Step 8 and closes it as unresolved
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether סומכוס accepted the pebble tradition (and applies it to כח כחו) or rejected it completely

steps.title: Back to the משנה: kicking or pebbles pays half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which says that an animal that was kicking, or sent pebbles flying from under its feet and broke vessels, pays חצי נזק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was kicking, or pebbles were flying out from under its feet, and it broke the vessels, the owner pays half damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. It is setting up a question about how that line should be read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line names two cases, kicking and flying pebbles, and gives both the same payment of חצי נזק. It does not say exactly how the two cases connect to each other. That gap is what the next step asks about.

keyTerms.meaning: Kicking
Pebbles kicked up by the animal
Flying or spraying out
Half the cost of the damage

phrases.english: If it was kicking,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ צְרוֹרוֹת מְנַתְּזִין מִתַּחַת רַגְלֶיהָ,
phrases.english: or pebbles were flying out from under its feet,
and it broke the vessels –
he pays half the damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה מְבַעֶטֶת אוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ צְרוֹרוֹת מְנַתְּזִין מִתַּחַת רַגְלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the questions about צרורות are closed, the גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal that kicked, or sent pebbles flying, and broke vessels: the owner pays חצי נזק

steps.title: How should this משנה line be read?
steps.stepSummary: The scholars ask what case the משנה is actually describing in this line.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was asked of them: what is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about the meaning of the משנה line it just quoted. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'kicking, or pebbles' could be read in more than one way. The גמרא wants to know exactly which case the משנה means when it gives חצי נזק. The next step lays out the two possible readings.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was asked of them': a question raised among the scholars
'How is it saying?': what exactly does it mean

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
How is it saying [this]?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ הֵיכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the משנה line quoted in Step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case the משנה is describing when it says 'kicking, or pebbles flying' pays חצי נזק

steps.title: Two possible readings of the kicking-and-pebbles line
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out both sides. Either the משנה gives חצי נזק even for normal pebbles, which is רבנן's view. Or it gives חצי נזק only for pebbles kicked up by a kick, which means normal pebbles pay full damage, which is סומכוס's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the משנה mean: if it kicked and damaged with the kick, or sent pebbles flying in the normal way, he pays half damage, so this is רבנן? Or does it mean: if it kicked and damaged with the kick, or sent pebbles flying because of a kick, he pays half damage, but pebbles in the normal way pay full damage, so this is סומכוס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is spelling out the question from the last step. It gives two different ways to read the same line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first reading, the word 'pebbles' is its own case: normal walking that kicks up pebbles. That fits רבנן, who say pebbles pay half. In the second reading, 'pebbles' is tied to the kick, so normal pebbles must pay full damage, and that is סומכוס's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Kicking. This is unusual behavior for an animal, a type of קרן.
Pebbles that fly out from under the animal's feet
In their normal way, the way animals usually walk
Because of
The תנא who holds that pebble damage pays full damage

phrases.english: Was it kicking and damaged with its kick,
or sent pebbles flying in the normal way —
he pays half damage, and it follows the Rabbis;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, הָיְתָה מְבַעֶטֶת וְהִזִּיקָה בְּבִיעוּטָהּ,
phrases.english: or perhaps: it was kicking and damaged with its kick,
or sent pebbles flying because of a kick —
he pays half damage,

phrases.aramaic: הָא כִּי אוֹרְחֵיהּ – מְשַׁלֵּם נֶזֶק שָׁלֵם,
phrases.english: but in its normal way, he pays full damage,
and whose view is it? It is Sumakhos.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the question asked in step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's 'pebbles' means normal pebbles (רבנן) or pebbles from a kick (סומכוס)

steps.title: Proof from the shard that broke a second vessel
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says that when a shard from a broken vessel breaks another vessel, the owner pays חצי נזק. סומכוס doesn't hold of חצי נזק for pebbles, so the משנה seems to follow רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear from the later part of the משנה: if the animal stepped on a vessel and broke it, and a piece fell on another vessel and broke it, he pays full damage for the first and half damage for the last. If this were סומכוס, does he hold of half damage?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question using a later line in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second vessel was broken by a flying piece, which is just like pebbles, and the משנה says to pay half. סומכוס says pebbles pay full damage. So it seems the whole משנה follows רבנן, which supports the first reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. This opens a proof from a source.
The later part of a משנה or ברייתא
It stepped on
A broken piece, a shard
Full damage payment

phrases.english: Come and hear from the later clause:
It stepped on a vessel and broke it,

phrases.aramaic: וְנָפַל הַשֶּׁבֶר עַל כְּלִי אַחֵר וּשְׁבָרוֹ –
phrases.english: and the shard fell on another vessel and broke it —
for the first he pays full damage,
and for the last, half damage.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סוֹמְכוֹס, מִי אִית לֵיהּ חֲצִי נֶזֶק?
phrases.english: And if it were Sumakhos, does he hold of half damage?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע מִסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question from step 12
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה follows רבנן, so 'pebbles' means normal pebbles
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה: a shard breaking a second vessel pays חצי נזק

steps.title: Rereading 'first' and 'second' so it fits סומכוס
steps.stepSummary: A possible way out: 'first' means the first vessel hit by a flying piece, and 'second' means a vessel hit by a piece of that one. סומכוס would pay full for כחו and half for כח כחו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: 'first' means the first one hit by flying pieces, and 'second' means the second one hit by flying pieces, and סומכוס makes a difference between its force and the force of its force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible answer that would let the משנה fit סומכוס after all. The next step will push it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, the vessel hit directly by a flying shard is כחו, so סומכוס would say full damage. A vessel hit by a piece of that vessel is כח כחו, and only there would he say half. That way סומכוס could have a חצי נזק case.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say. This brings up a possible answer.
Flying out, being sent flying
Its force: damage from something the animal itself sent moving
The force of its force: damage from something sent moving by something the animal sent moving

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'first' does NOT mean the vessel the animal stepped on. It means the first vessel hit by a flying piece.

phrases.english: And if you would say: 'first' means first of the flying,
phrases.notes: He means the first vessel hit by a flying piece, which is really the second vessel to break.

phrases.english: and 'second' means second of the flying;
and for Sumakhos there is a difference
between its force and the force of its force;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible way to deflect the proof in step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the משנה must follow רבנן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes 'first' is the vessel stepped on. It could mean the first vessel hit by a flying piece, with half damage only for כח כחו.

steps.title: Then רב אשי's question would already be answered
steps.stepSummary: The possible way out from step 14 is rejected. If the משנה followed סומכוס and gave half for כח כחו, רב אשי could have answered his own question about כח כחו right from this משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what about רב אשי's question: according to סומכוס, is the force of its force like its force or not? Let him answer it from here, that it is not like its force!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the answer from the last step by pointing to רב אשי's unanswered question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי asked whether סומכוס treats כח כחו like כחו, and it ended in תיקו. If this משנה clearly followed סומכוס and paid only half for כח כחו, that question would have had an easy answer. So it seems the reading from step 14 can't be right, and the proof that the משנה follows רבנן would stand again. Step 16 answers this difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so. This opens a difficulty with what was just suggested.
Asked, raised a question
Is like, is compared to
Resolve, settle the question

steps.whatToRemember: The סיפא's חצי נזק for the shard can't be explained by סומכוס's כחו and כח כחו split, because then רב אשי's question would already be settled.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an unresolved question (רב אשי's תיקו) can be used to reject a reading of a משנה.

phrases.english: But then, that which Rav Ashi asked:
phrases.notes: This is the question from step 8, which ended in תיקו.

phrases.english: the force of its force, according to Sumakhos —

phrases.aramaic: כְּכֹחוֹ דָּמֵי אוֹ לָאו כְּכֹחוֹ דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: is it like its force, or not like its force?
Let him resolve it that it is not like its force!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּבָעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the possible answer offered in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'first' and 'second' mean first and second of the flying pieces, according to סומכוס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה showed that סומכוס gives half for כח כחו, רב אשי's question would be answered. But it stayed a תיקו, so the משנה can't be read that way.

steps.title: רב אשי reads the משנה like the Rabbis and asks a different question
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the משנה according to רבנן. His question on it is whether pebbles kicked up by a kick count as a שינוי, so the owner pays only רביע נזק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי explains the משנה according to רבנן, and he asks his question this way: if the animal was kicking and did damage with its kick, or it scattered pebbles in its normal way, the owner pays half damage. That would mean that pebbles kicked up because of a kick pay only a quarter of the damage, because there is a change from normal behavior.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the difficulty from step 15. רב אשי never read this משנה like סומכוס, so it could not answer his question about כח כחו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבנן, normal pebbles already pay חצי נזק. So the open question becomes whether a kick, which is unusual behavior, lowers pebble damage even further, to רביע נזק. Here the גמרא presents the first way to read the משנה, the one where a kick does make a difference.

keyTerms.meaning: he explains it as following (a certain opinion)
in their normal way
a quarter of the damage
a change from the animal's normal behavior

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the kick itself with pebbles kicked up by a kick. If the animal damages directly with its kick, that is like קרן and pays half. The question here is only about pebbles that fly because of a kick.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi explains it according to the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: "It" is our משנה. So for him it says nothing about סומכוס's view.

phrases.english: and he asks it this way:
If it was kicking and did damage with its kick,
or pebbles in their normal way –
half damage.
But pebbles because of a kick –
a quarter of the damage, and a change from normal behavior counts;

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי כְּרַבָּנַן מוֹקֵי לַהּ, וּבָעֵי לַהּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty from step 15 by moving רב אשי's reading of the משנה to רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the opinion: the משנה follows רבנן, so it cannot settle a question about סומכוס.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה followed סומכוס, so רב אשי should have learned the answer about כח כחו from it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב אשי reads the משנה like רבנן. His question on it is only whether a kick creates a שינוי for pebbles.

steps.title: The other side of רב אשי's question, left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The other possibility is that kicked-up pebbles also pay חצי נזק, so a kick makes no difference for pebbles. The question stays unresolved (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps the משנה means: if the animal was kicking and did damage with its kick, or scattered pebbles because of a kick, the owner pays half damage, and the change from normal behavior makes no difference. The question stands unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second way to read the משנה and then ends רב אשי's question with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, the משנה's word "pebbles" means pebbles kicked up by a kick, and they still pay only half. That would show that a שינוי does not lower pebble damage below half. The גמרא cannot decide between the two readings.

keyTerms.meaning: or perhaps
a change from normal behavior makes no difference
the question stands unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבנן, normal pebbles pay חצי נזק. Whether pebbles kicked up by a kick pay a quarter or still pay half is left unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Or perhaps,
if it was kicking and did damage with its kick,
or pebbles because of a kick –
half damage, and a change from normal behavior makes no difference?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא, הָיְתָה מְבַעֶטֶת וְהִזִּיקָה בְּבִיעוּטָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the question begun in step 16 and closes it with תיקו.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether kicked-up pebbles count as a שינוי and pay only רביע נזק is not decided.

steps.title: An animal that must scatter pebbles but kicks them up anyway
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל asks about an animal walking where it cannot avoid scattering pebbles, but it kicked and scattered them and caused damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל asked רבי אמי, and some say he asked רבי חייא בר אבא: if an animal was walking in a place where it is impossible to walk without scattering pebbles, and it kicked, scattered pebbles, and caused damage, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. It builds on the topic of pebbles kicked up by a kick, and the next step will lay out its two sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the pebbles would have flown no matter what, because the ground forces it. The question is whether the kick still matters when the scattering itself was going to happen anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: it is impossible
scattering, making things fly
what is the law?
and some say

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel asked Rabbi Ami,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ מֵרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: and some say, Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba:
If it was walking in a place

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהּ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מְנַתֶּזֶת,
phrases.english: where it is impossible for it unless it scatters pebbles,
and it kicked, scattered pebbles, and caused damage, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related question about pebbles kicked up by a kick.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a kick still count as unusual when the animal would have scattered pebbles anyway?

steps.title: Two ways to see it, left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: Since the animal could not avoid scattering pebbles, maybe this is its normal way. Or maybe these particular pebbles flew because of a kick. The question stays unresolved (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it could not avoid it, perhaps scattering is its normal way. Or perhaps, in any case, right now the pebbles flew because of a kick? The question stands unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two sides of רבי אבא בר ממל's question and ends with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one looks at the situation: scattering pebbles there is normal, so the law is the same as regular pebbles. Side two looks at what actually happened: these pebbles flew because of a kick, so the law is that of kicked-up pebbles.

keyTerms.meaning: it is its normal way
now, in any case

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַהּ – אוֹרְחַיהּ הוּא;
phrases.english: Since it is impossible for it otherwise – it is its normal way;
or perhaps, now in any case,
it scattered the pebbles because of a kick?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַהּ אוֹרְחַיהּ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the question from step 18 and leaves it unresolved.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a kick matters when the animal would have scattered pebbles anyway is not decided.

steps.title: Kicked-up pebbles in רשות הרבים: like קרן or like רגל?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא whether pebbles kicked up in רשות הרבים are compared to קרן, so the owner is liable, or count as a תולדה of רגל, so the owner is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא: if an animal was walking in the public domain, and it kicked, scattered pebbles, and caused damage, what is the law? Do we compare it to קרן, so the owner is liable? Or perhaps it is a תולדה of רגל, so the owner is exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens, this time about where the damage happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רגל and its תולדות are exempt in רשות הרבים, but קרן is liable everywhere. A kick is like קרן, but the damage was done by pebbles, which are a תולדה of רגל. So the question is which side wins.

keyTerms.meaning: the public domain
goring, damage done on purpose; liable even in the public domain
a sub-type of רגל (trampling)
exempt

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked Rabbi Zeira:
If it was walking in the public domain,
and it kicked, scattered pebbles, and caused damage, what is the law?
Do we compare it to goring – and it is liable,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא תּוֹלָדָה דְרֶגֶל הוּא – וּפְטוּרָה?
phrases.english: or perhaps it is a sub-type of trampling – and it is exempt?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about kicked-up pebbles, now in the public domain.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are kicked-up pebbles in רשות הרבים treated like קרן (liable) or like רגל (exempt)?

steps.title: רבי זירא: it is a תולדה of רגל
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that it makes sense to treat it as a תולדה of רגל, so the owner is exempt in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: it makes sense that it is a תולדה of רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers רבי ירמיה's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though a kick was involved, the damage came through pebbles, which belong under רגל. So the exemption of רגל in the public domain applies here too.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense, it is logical

steps.whatToRemember: Pebbles kicked up in רשות הרבים are a תולדה of רגל, so the owner is exempt there.

phrases.english: He said to him: It makes sense
that it is a sub-type of trampling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִסְתַּבְּרָא, תּוֹלָדָה דְרֶגֶל הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a תולדה of רגל, so the owner is exempt in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Pebbles flung in the public area that damage in a private area
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks a follow-up: what if the animal flung the pebbles in רשות הרבים, but they landed and caused damage in רשות היחיד?
steps.simpleTranslation: If the animal flung pebbles in the public domain and they caused damage in a private domain, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא another question that builds on the answer we just saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא just ruled that kicked-up pebbles count as a תולדה of רגל, so the owner is exempt in רשות הרבים. Now the case is split between two places: the pebbles start in רשות הרבים but do their damage in רשות היחיד. Which place decides the law?

keyTerms.meaning: It (the animal) flung or sprayed pebbles
A private domain
What is the law?

phrases.english: It flung [pebbles] in the public domain
phrases.notes: רבי ירמיה is still the one asking רבי זירא, just as in the step before.

phrases.english: and they caused damage in a private domain, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתִּיזָה בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים וְהִזִּיקָה בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question built on רבי זירא's answer that pebbles are a תולדה of רגל
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do we follow the place where the pebbles were flung or the place where they caused damage?

steps.title: No lifting here, so no placing either
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers with a picture borrowed from the laws of שבת: if the starting point carries no liability, the landing point cannot create any. So the owner is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There is no lifting here, so is there placing here?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers that the owner is exempt, because the place where the pebbles started is what counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of שבת, carrying needs a עקירה (lifting from one place) and a הנחה (putting down in another). רבי זירא uses this picture: the pebbles were flung in רשות הרבים, where there is no liability. So where they landed cannot make the owner liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Lifting up; the starting point of an action
Putting down; the ending point of an action

phrases.english: He said to him:
There is no lifting here,
phrases.notes: These are words from the laws of שבת. He means there is no liability where the pebbles started.

phrases.english: is there placing here?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עֲקִירָה אֵין כָּאן, הַנָּחָה יֵשׁ כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The owner is exempt, because we follow the place the pebbles were flung (רשות הרבים).

steps.title: A ברייתא says the owner is liable even in the public area
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes a ברייתא: an animal walking that flings pebbles makes the owner liable, both in רשות היחיד and in רשות הרבים. That seems to go against רבי זירא's earlier ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: If it was walking along the way and flung pebbles, whether in a private domain or in the public domain, the owner is liable. Isn't this a case where the pebbles were flung and caused damage in the public domain?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי זירא's first ruling (step 21) with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא had said that pebbles in רשות הרבים are a תולדה of רגל, so the owner is exempt. The ברייתא says the owner is liable even in רשות הרבים. The simple reading is that the whole event happened in רשות הרבים, which would contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him from a source
Liable
What, is it not...? (pushing for the simple reading of a source)

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
If it was walking along the way and flung [pebbles],

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: whether in a private domain or in the public domain, he is liable.
What, is it not that it flung them in the public domain
and they caused damage in the public domain?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: הָיְתָה מְהַלֶּכֶת בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְהִתִּיזָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי זירא's ruling from step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's ruling that pebbles in רשות הרבים are a תולדה of רגל and exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes the owner liable in רשות הרבים, which seems to mean pebble damage there is paid.

steps.title: The ברייתא means they landed in a private area
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the ברייתא is talking about pebbles flung in רשות הרבים that caused damage in רשות היחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it flung them in the public domain and they caused damage in a private domain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends his first ruling by reading the ברייתא as a split case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the damage happened in רשות היחיד, the ברייתא no longer contradicts his ruling about damage inside רשות הרבים. But this answer only works if pebbles that land in רשות היחיד make the owner liable, and that is exactly what he just denied in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: No (rejecting the questioner's reading)

phrases.english: No, it flung them in the public domain
and they caused damage in a private domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, הִתִּיזָה בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, וְהִזִּיקָה בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about pebbles flung and causing damage in רשות הרבים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about pebbles flung in רשות הרבים that caused damage in רשות היחיד.

steps.title: But you just said that case is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה points out that רבי זירא's answer clashes with what he said in step 23, that flinging in רשות הרבים exempts the owner even if the damage is in רשות היחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you say: there is no lifting here, so is there placing here?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה catches a contradiction between רבי זירא's answer and his own earlier ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23, רבי זירא said the split case is exempt. In step 25, he used the split case to explain a ברייתא that says liable. Both cannot be true.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't you say? (quoting someone's own words back to him)

phrases.english: But didn't you say:

phrases.aramaic: עֲקִירָה אֵין כָּאן, הַנָּחָה יֵשׁ כָּאן!
phrases.english: There is no lifting here, so is there placing here!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמְרַתְּ: עֲקִירָה אֵין כָּאן, הַנָּחָה יֵשׁ כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי זירא's answer in step 25 against his ruling in step 23
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His answer assumes the split case is liable, but he had ruled it exempt.

steps.title: רבי זירא retracts
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says he takes back his statement that the split case is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I retract.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא admits the ברייתא proves him wrong on the split case, and he changes his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He takes back only the 'no lifting, no placing' ruling. Pebbles flung in רשות הרבים that damage in רשות היחיד make the owner liable. His first ruling still stands: pebbles flung and causing damage inside רשות הרבים are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: I retract; I take back what I said

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא does not take back everything. He keeps the ruling that pebble damage entirely inside רשות הרבים is exempt. He only drops the claim that the place where the pebbles started decides the law.

phrases.english: He said to him: I retract.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲדַרִי בִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concedes the contradiction raised in step 26

steps.title: The broken vessel case challenges רבי זירא again
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes a משנה: an animal steps on a vessel, and a broken piece flies and breaks a second vessel. A ברייתא on that משנה says that in רשות הרבים the owner is exempt for the first vessel but liable for the second. That seems to say flung pieces in רשות הרבים are paid for.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: If it stepped on a vessel and broke it, and the broken piece fell on another vessel and broke it, he pays full damage for the first and half damage for the last. And a ברייתא teaches on this: When is this said? In the injured party's domain. But in the public domain, he is exempt for the first and liable for the last. Isn't this a case where it was flung and caused damage in the public domain?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה brings a second source against רבי זירא's first ruling (step 21).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking the first vessel by stepping on it is plain רגל, so in רשות הרבים the owner is exempt. The second vessel was broken by a flying piece, which is like pebbles, and the ברייתא says he is liable even in רשות הרבים. That contradicts the ruling that pebbles in רשות הרבים are exempt as a תולדה of רגל.

steps.title: The piece landed in a private area
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא gives the same answer as before: the broken piece was flung in רשות הרבים and broke the second vessel in רשות היחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it was flung in the public domain and caused damage in a private domain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends his ruling by reading the ברייתא as a split case again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps his ruling about damage entirely inside רשות הרבים safe. Once again, the answer only works if the split case makes the owner liable.

steps.title: Again: but you said that case is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה again reminds רבי זירא that he ruled the split case exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you say: there is no lifting here, so is there placing here?!
steps.whatsHappening: The same contradiction comes up again with this second source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as in step 26, the answer depends on the split case being liable. That clashes with the 'no lifting, no placing' ruling.

steps.title: רבי זירא retracts again
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא again says he takes back his statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I retract.
steps.whatsHappening: The second exchange ends the same way as the first: רבי זירא retracts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sources now show that pebbles flung in רשות הרבים which damage in רשות היחיד make the owner liable. The 'no lifting, no placing' idea is dropped. Pebble damage entirely inside רשות הרבים is still exempt.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא keeps his ruling that pebbles kicked up in רשות הרבים are a תולדה of רגל and exempt there. If they land and cause damage in רשות היחיד, the owner is liable.

phrases.english: He said to him: I retract.

steps.title: Another challenge begins: is that really so?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה opens a new challenge with "Is that so?!" He is questioning the claim that an owner is פטור for pieces his animal flings in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. "Is that so?!" signals that a new challenge is coming against the idea that flung pieces in רשות הרבים are פטור. The source behind the challenge comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twice already, רבי זירא answered by moving the damage into רשות היחיד, and twice he was reminded of his split-case ruling. This word starts a fresh attack on the same claim. It shows the doubt about "flung pieces in רשות הרבים are פטור" has not been settled yet.

keyTerms.meaning: "Is that so?" An opening word that signals the גמרא is about to challenge a statement.
Pebbles or pieces flung by an animal's movement, which cause damage indirectly.
Exempt, not required to pay.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read אִינִי as a real request for information. It is a challenge, and the proof behind it is quoted right after.
